messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> P1: High error rate on QuantumMed VPC auth (dedicated pool qm-prod). Observed tls/mTLS handshake failures against tenant-auth-proxy. Paging oncall. https://internal.incidents/1873000000 :rotating_light:
infra-oncall (Alejandra): I'm on it, grabbing logs from the qm-prod pool now.
alice.k (Oncall SRE): seeing spikes in 502/503 from auth-proxy behind envoy. 10k failures in last 5m, p99 latency for handshake is high.
ben.r (Auth eng): any change in cert rotation yesterday? customer claimed rotation last night.
jenn (CS): Jenn from CS — Quantum Med reports service errors starting ~22:09 UTC, they see failures in their sidecar connections. They applied a new cert chain earlier.
alice.k (Oncall SRE): grabbing a sample tls error from auth-proxy logs:
```
2026-07-15T22:12:34Z auth-proxy ERROR handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (depth=0)
2026-07-15T22:12:34Z envoy WARN TLS: remote error: handshake failure, verify error: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
ben.r (Auth eng): that stack looks like missing intermediate CA in the client cert chain. Our verifier expects full chain from client. If customer sent leaf only, envoy fails the chain build.
matt.d (Platform PM): impact scope? only qm-prod pool/tenant? any cross-tenant effects?
alice.k (Oncall SRE): confirmed isolated to qm-prod dedicated pool and the qm tenant in hosted-vpc. No other tenants showing TLS errors. Tenant isolation intact.
jenn (CS): Customer says they updated a cert yesterday via their internal CA tool; they can re-send full bundle but will take 30-45m.
ben.r (Auth eng): short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to upload full chain (recommended). 2) we can temporarily accept partial chains at verifier layer (risk: weaker verification). 3) fallback to bearer-token auth for qm if enabled. Which is least risk?
alice.k (Oncall SRE): can we toggle the verifier to allow building chain from system CAs? config is in auth-config CM `auth-verifier:allow_partial_chain`. Currently false.
ben.r (Auth eng): yes, we can set it true for that tenant by patching tenant config and reload auth-proxy. Here's the command:
```
kubectl -n auth-staging patch configmap tenant-qm --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/allow_partial_chain","value":"true"}]'
kubectl -n auth-staging rollout restart deployment tenant-auth-proxy-qm
```
alice.k (Oncall SRE): starting patch for qm-prod in staging to smoke test, will then apply to prod with a quick rollback plan.
deploy-bot: Deployment tenant-auth-proxy-qm restarted (uid: d4f2a7).
alice.k (Oncall SRE): patched in staging, tests show immediate drop in handshake errors for sample clients. Will apply to prod in 2 mins with monitoring.
matt.d (Platform PM): note we need an SLO/rollback threshold — if error rate increases elsewhere, revert.
alice.k (Oncall SRE): applying to prod now.
deploy-bot: Deployment tenant-auth-proxy-qm prod restarted (uid: a9c3b2).
alice.k (Oncall SRE): prod patch done. qm-prod handshake errors dropped from 93% to 2% within 90s. Token auth fallback also enabled temporarily for older clients.
jenn (CS): Confirmed with Quantum Med—they can now connect and are running acceptance tests. They will send the full chain in ~35m and rotate again.
ben.r (Auth eng): mitigation notes: we allowed partial chain acceptance for tenant qm. This reduces verification strictness — track any anomalous leaf CAs accepted. Will add a temporary allowlist for known issuer thumbprint qm-ca-thumbprint:AB12..
sasha (next-oncall): I'm taking the handoff for the next 4 hours. Key actions: 1) verify customer uploads full chain and we revert allow_partial_chain to false after validation, 2) rotate any temporary tokens we issued as fallback, 3) prepare postmortem.
alice.k (Oncall SRE): handing off — logs, commands, and the patch snippet in pinned messages. Current status: degraded -> mitigated, customer verified.
incident-bot: Incident marked as acknowledged by alice.k, severity downgraded to P2 after mitigation.
matt.d (Platform PM): Post-incident tasks: - engineering to add a verifier metric for partial-chain hits - docs for tenants about cert bundles - improvement to rollout for per-tenant verifier flags. Ben, can you own the follow-up?
ben.r (Auth eng): I’ll own follow-up and the postmortem. Will coordinate with Jenn to confirm the customer provided the full chain and then schedule a patch to remove allow_partial_chain and run a verification sweep.
jenn (CS): I'll coordinate customer timeline and get the bundle.
sasha (next-oncall): Handoff note: I'll monitor for 1hr then tag infra-oncall if anything reappears. Leaving alert thresholds lowered to 5 failures/min for 30m.
alice.k (Oncall SRE): ack handoff, leaving runbook entry: `qm_prod_partial_chain_mitigation` with steps and rollback command.
ben.r (Auth eng): sample rollback command if needed:
```
kubectl -n auth-staging patch configmap tenant-qm --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/allow_partial_chain","value":"false"}]'
kubectl -n auth-staging rollout restart deployment tenant-auth-proxy-qm
```
alice.k (Oncall SRE): closing timeline notes. First seen 2026-07-15T22:09Z, mitigation applied 22:17Z, customer verified 22:22Z.
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Summary: partial client cert chain from customer caused mTLS verification failures for Quantum Med tenant; temporary per-tenant verifier relaxation applied; full-chain requested and pending; postmortem owners: ben.r (Auth eng), jenn (CS). :white_check_mark:
